title: What happened in AI — Oct 30, 2026
intro: The day's sharpest signal came from the field: an unsandboxed Claude Code run with seven parallel subagents spilled into a developer's Mac, and builders answered with hooks, checks and tighter review.

Underneath, cost and trust layers moved too: OpenRouter now routes on speed and reliability as well as price, Google Cloud spend caps are generally available, and new proposals tie agent actions to verified identity.
highlights: A Claude Code auto-mode run with seven parallel subagents and no sandbox made a Mac talk; the report traces it to the agents' tests.
OpenRouter's new default router rewards fast, reliable providers, not just the cheapest.
Google Cloud spend caps on Budgets are generally available and do not delete resources.
Turnbook reports 91.8% on LongMemEval from 3.1k memory tokens per question.
OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal for AI training preferences.

categories.name: Coding agents need guardrails, not trust
categories.summary: Unsandboxed parallel agents leaked side effects into the host, and teams are answering with hooks, pre-ship checks and focused review.

articles.title: A Claude Code agent's test escaped into my Mac. I only noticed because it talked
articles.summary: Seven parallel Claude Code subagents in auto mode, with no sandbox, made a Mac read JSON aloud; the incident report traces it to the agents' own test run.

articles.title: Show HN: Claude Code guards built from my agent's repeated mistakes
articles.summary: Seven Claude Code hooks and pre-ship checks, each built from a logged agent mistake, with tests that prove each one blocks.

articles.title: How (not) to use AI for pull requests and code reviews
articles.summary: Agent-written PR descriptions list every change and run long; the author argues reviewers should be pointed at what matters, not read everything.

articles.title: What Claude Code's 30-second agent summary call costs, read from the binary
articles.summary: Reading the Claude Code binary, the author finds each background agent's transcript is sent to the model about every 30 seconds to write a 3-5 word status line, and prices one call at Opus 5.5 rates.

categories.name: Context and memory under a token budget
categories.summary: Two open-source tools attack agent context cost from different ends: cheaper memory writes and smarter selection of what enters the window.

articles.title: Same agent-memory accuracy with 8x fewer tokens by changing the embedding model
articles.summary: Turnbook stores conversations verbatim with zero model tokens at save time and reports 91.8% on LongMemEval from 3.1k tokens of memory per question.

articles.title: Show HN: Omneum – Local, text-blind context control plane for AI agents
articles.summary: Omneum selects high-utility context under a token budget, scoring source reliability and claim support to counter context rot.

categories.name: Inference routing and cloud spend controls
categories.summary: Routing and billing layers are moving from lowest price to price plus speed and reliability, with hard caps on runaway spend.

articles.title: OpenRouter rebuilt provider routing for better, faster inference
articles.summary: OpenRouter's default router now weighs speed, throughput and reliability alongside price, so better providers win more traffic with no client code change.

articles.title: Innovate on your own business terms: Google Cloud spend caps now generally available
articles.summary: Spend caps on Google Cloud Budgets are generally available, built to stop runaway costs without deleting resources.

articles.title: Show HN: Spinf-serve – inference server for bulk scoring and decisions
articles.summary: spinf-serve reads content once and scores many questions in one pass as option probabilities, on one 24 GB GPU behind an OpenAI-compatible API (Apache 2.0).

categories.name: Agent identity, authorization and policy
categories.summary: Builders are proposing ways to prove who an agent acts for and cap what it can do, while OpenAI backs a robots.txt signal for training preferences.

articles.title: Personal Agent's Voice Security
articles.summary: OpenAVT carries cryptographic identity and signed customer permissions through a phone call's audio so a business can verify an agent before acting.

articles.title: Show HN: Send21 – Crypto pay links an AI agent can create but can't spend
articles.summary: Send21 lets an agent create crypto payment drafts through a scoped API but not spend; the human pays from their own wallet.

articles.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
articles.summary: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal for website AI training preferences, for participating providers.

categories.name: Multi-agent behavior and evals
categories.summary: New testbeds probe agents in groups and on deterministic tasks instead of relying on LLM judges.

articles.title: What YC's Minecraft and Mindustry agent swarms show about multi-agent teams
articles.summary: A write-up of Y Combinator and Olam Labs runs with 50 agents in Minecraft and Mindustry, pitting GPT-6.1 Sol teams against Claude Opus 5.5 teams, turns each failure into a check.

articles.title: Show HN: Navital Gym – open environments for testing AI agents on Indian tasks
articles.summary: Navital Gym offers deterministic, rule-graded environments for Indian tasks such as UPI, GST and trip planning, with no LLM judge.
